A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in idiopathic portal hypotension, aberrant vessels are the most important factor for maintaining the hepatic circulation.
the portal blood flow is diverted to the aberrant vessels, which connect the portal vein and the sinusoids, and the liver is protected from collapse by blockage of the peripheral portal veins.
in idiopathic portal hypertention, the hepatic tissue is preserved from collapse by the presence of intrahepatically located aberrant vessels which drain the portal blood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found that aberrant vessels are a common finding in noncirrhotics with portal hypertension, and that these aberrant vessels are not the same as portovenous shunt vessels.
